preconditions.description: Input constraints: n is the number of vertices, l is the maximum path length, and w is the maximum path weight.
The tree has exactly n-1 edges, where edges are parsed from input.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p < (i + 1) <= n and 0 <= weight <= 10**4 for i, (p, weight) in enumerate(edges))
preconditions.description: Each edge connects vertex (i+1) to p with weight in [0, 10^4].

postconditions.description: The output is the count of unordered vertex pairs (v, u) where v < u and they are close, defined as having a path of length ≤ l and a path of weight ≤ w between them.

postconditions.expression: count_close_pairs(n, l, w, edges) == sum(1 for v in range(1, n) for u in range(v + 1, n + 1) if are_close(v, u, n, l, w, edges))
postconditions.description: The count is the sum of 1 for every valid pair (v, u) where v < u and they are close.

postconditions.expression: are_close(v, u, n, l, w, edges) == (path_length(v, u, edges) <= l and path_weight(v, u, edges) <= w)
postconditions.description: Two vertices v and u are close if there exists a path between them with length ≤ l and weight ≤ w.
